what: A change of the crate graph was one bool: adding one crate (a `cfg(test)` twin) was indistinguishable from changing every crate, so name resolution ran every crate from empty and the impls maintainer swept every crate.
cost: the reason a switch of request cost a whole lowering even where the crates were kept; an hour to find every reader of the bool before a field could be added
cause: the note was made when a database held one plan, so a graph change was always the whole graph
whys: a maintainer reads `written.crates` to decide whether its state stands
the write methods note `Crates` whenever the graph's content ID moves
the content ID is of the whole list, so it cannot say which crate
class: a delta said as a flag
prevention: `Written::crates_added` names crates added; `Crate::create_added` and `base_db::add_crates` are the only way blaze-lower adds a crate; base-db's test `a_crate_added_beside_the_graph_names_itself_and_not_the_graph` holds the note
fix: written in this lane (not yet built)
state: open until the round's build and tests pass
